title: Man killed in police shooting in Saskatoon was shot and wounded in February confrontation
subtitle: Ronald Glen Herman had been wounded during a confrontation with Saskatoon police in February. Regina police has completed its investigation into that incident.
article: A man who was fatally shot in a confrontation with Saskatoon police last week had previously been wounded by officers in a February incident when he was allegedly armed with an airsoft gun.
According to an online obituary, which has since been deleted, the man was Ronald Herman, 36.

Police said last week that a 36-year-old man wanted by La Loche RCMP was believed to be in the 1300 block of Avenue E North and had a gun. He was suspected of breaching release conditions and of removing his electronic monitoring device, police said in a media release last week.
The man allegedly pointed a gun at officers while he was inside the building and while outside of it, and the tactical support unit then entered the building, the previous statement said.
"As we have previously released, it was at that time they were confronted by the suspect and the fatal shooting occurred."
The incident on Thursday evening took place while parent-teacher interviews were being conducted across the street at Mayfair Community School.

Herman faced several charges in connection with a Feb. 23 incident in which he was shot by officers in the area of Avenue U South and 22nd Street West. He was treated in hospital and released into custody. According to court documents, he was allegedly armed with an airsoft gun.
Regina police had been asked to investigate the Feb. 23 non-fatal shooting.

"Our investigation into the Feb. 23rd police-involved, non-fatal shooting has been completed and sent to the appointed independent observers. The process in such matters has us submitting our entire investigative package for review. Last week's events do not change that," a police spokesperson said in an email.

Saskatoon provincial court records say Herman was expected to next appear in court on Nov. 10 and a bench warrant was in effect. A bench warrant can be issued by a judge for the arrest of someone to ensure they appear in court if they have failed to appear.

Last January, RCMP sought the public's help locating Herman, who was wanted on several charges stemming from a December 2020 incident. At the time, RCMP described him as "dangerous and a high risk to reoffend."

Two independent observers have been appointed by the province and Regina police will conduct an independent investigation into the fatal shooting, with the Saskatchewan Serious Incident Response Team in an observer role.
In a release issued late Monday afternoon, Regina police asked that anyone with information or video evidence related to the shooting contact police at 306-777-6500.
Neither Saskatoon police nor Regina police have confirmed the identity of the man who died.
Saskatoon police, on behalf of Regina police, issued a media release Monday asking any member of the public who witnessed or has video relevant to the incident to contact the Regina Police Service.
